title: ERIS vs Fireflies: a meeting AI assistant today, or meetings inside one business system with local AI
content_html:
ERIS vs Fireflies: a meeting AI assistant, or meetings inside one business system with local AI

In the ERIS vs Fireflies choice, Fireflies is a dedicated AI meeting assistant. According to its website in November 2026, Fireflies transcribes, summarises, searches and analyses team conversations from Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and other platforms. ERIS, by Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl), is a different kind of product. It is one business system, and meeting notes are one part of it next to tasks, documents and CRM. ERIS runs with a local AI model, either on the company's own servers or hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider. ERIS is in beta now.

What Fireflies is good at

Fireflies is built around one job: making meetings searchable and useful after they end. Everything below is how its own website described it in November 2026.

  • Meeting notes from the tools teams already use. Fireflies says it transcribes, summarises, searches and analyses team conversations. It records meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and other platforms.
  • Recording without a bot in the call. Its Chrome extension records, transcribes and summarises Google Meet calls without a bot joining the meeting. The extension runs in Google Chrome, Brave and Microsoft Edge.
  • Phone calls too. Fireflies transcribes calls from dialers such as Aircall and RingCentral. It also offers an API (a connection other software can use) for processing audio files.
  • Notes go where people work. It sends notes and alerts into Slack channels. It sends meeting notes and transcripts to applicant tracking systems such as Greenhouse and Lever.
  • Meeting data in other systems. Through its API, overviews, action items, keywords and topics can be pulled into a CRM, a project tracker or a data warehouse.
  • Security and compliance information. Fireflies' website lists security and compliance certifications and storage options. Check its website for the current list and what each plan includes.

For a team that only wants meeting notes, connected to the tools it already runs, Fireflies is a strong and mature choice. To find out where meeting audio and transcripts are stored and processed, check Fireflies' own terms.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS puts meetings inside one system for the whole business, with one AI assistant across all of it.

Meetings are one app, not the whole product. ERIS records and transcribes meetings on Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, records Google Meet without a bot joining the call, and transcribes calls from phone dialers. Next to meetings, ERIS has a task manager, project management, document management, document signing and CRM in one system, and new apps arrive almost every week.

One data layer and one assistant. ERIS has one login, one data layer and one audit trail across its apps. The ERIS Assistant answers plain-language questions from company data, documents and the internal knowledge base, and names its source. So a question can draw on a meeting, the tasks that came out of it and the customer record in the CRM, without moving data between separate tools.

A local AI model in both deployment options. ERIS has two deployment options. It runs on the company's own servers, or it is hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider, for companies without their own hardware. Both always use a local AI model, and no outside AI provider receives client data in either option. In the on-premise option, meeting data never leaves the building.

Answers limited by access, and every action logged. The ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. Every question and every AI action is logged: who asked, which data was used, what it did and the result. A refused access is logged like every other question.

Instructions inside content stay content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content, never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden instructions meant to steer an AI).

ERIS vs Fireflies: which one should you pick

You only need meeting notes, sent into Slack, an applicant tracking system or your own software through an API. Pick Fireflies. It is a dedicated meeting assistant with those connections, and its website lists security and compliance certifications, so check that the ones you need are covered.

Your meeting audio and company data may not go to an outside AI provider, and you want meetings, tasks, documents and CRM in one system. Pick ERIS. It suits companies that cannot or will not send their data to outside cloud or AI providers, including the hosted option for companies without their own hardware. Whether a deployment meets the GDPR (the EU data protection rules), the EU AI Act or NIS2 (the EU cybersecurity rules) depends on the use case and is assessed per deployment.

If you are still comparing AI assistants, look at tools that work across company data rather than meetings alone.

FAQ

What hardware do I need to run ERIS with local AI?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU (graphics processing unit) server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and existing servers are not always enough. Running it on your own premises costs hardware, maintenance and updates. Local AI reads and searches company documents and is not trained on them.

Do I need my own IT team to run ERIS?

Not necessarily. A company without its own IT team or hardware can choose ERIS hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider, still with a local AI model. A company that runs ERIS on its own premises takes on the hardware, maintenance and updates.

Can ERIS connect to the software we already use?

ERIS records meetings on Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams and transcribes calls from phone dialers. It brings meetings, tasks, project management, documents, document signing and CRM into one system with one data layer, so less data has to move between separate tools. If you need ERIS to work with a specific tool, ask Upward when you request beta access.
